en.name: Christ the King
en.summary: The final Sunday of the liturgical year, proclaiming Christ's kingship over all creation, instituted in 1925 amid rising secular nationalism.
en.body: The Solemnity of Christ the King closes the liturgical year on its final Sunday, proclaiming Christ's sovereignty over all creation, individuals, families, societies, and nations alike, not as a temporal political ruler but as the one to whom all authority in heaven and on earth ultimately belongs. Pope Pius XI instituted the feast in 1925, explicitly responding to the rise of secular nationalism, atheistic communism, and fascism across interwar Europe, intending the feast as a counterweight reminding Christians that no earthly power held the ultimate claim on their allegiance. Its position as the final Sunday before Advent begins gives it a fittingly eschatological character, looking forward to the final establishment of Christ's kingdom at the end of time even as the liturgical year itself draws to a close.
